# ScopeBnB

> ScopeBnB rents a world-class remote astrophotography telescope under Bortle 1 dark skies at Starfront Observatories in Rockwood, Texas. Anyone, anywhere can capture deep-sky images without owning equipment.

ScopeBnB gives you a professional imaging rig under some of the darkest skies in the continental United States (Bortle 1, roughly 270 clear nights a year). You book online and choose how you want to work:

- **Managed imaging**: our team frames and captures your chosen target and delivers the session's calibrated light frames plus calibration frames (darks and flats) as 16-bit FITS to your dashboard within 24 hours. No experience needed. Priced by how dark the sky is that night, from $65 to $100 per night.
- **Remote control (N.I.N.A.)**: rent the rig and drive it yourself, pointing at any target you like. Sold only as a fixed block of consecutive nights at a flat rate (no single nights, no moon-based pricing): 3 nights for $150, or a full week of 7 nights for a flat $300 (the most popular, the best value).
- **Integrated image add-on ($25)**: optional processing where we calibrate, stack and finish your data into a ready-to-stretch image.

The rig is a wide-field setup (about 3° × 2° field of view), ideal for large nebulae and rich star fields. There is no subscription; you only pay when you book. Bad-weather nights are automatically rescheduled at no extra cost (weather guarantee).

Location: Starfront Observatories, 1724 County Road 244, Rockwood, TX 76873 (approx. 31.55° N, 99.38° W, elevation 472 m). Contact: contact@scopebnb.com

## Key pages
- [Home](https://scopebnb.com/): what ScopeBnB is and how it works
- [Book a night](https://scopebnb.com/book): choose managed or remote, pick your nights, choose a target
- [Pricing](https://scopebnb.com/pricing): nightly managed tiers, the remote 3-night and 7-night packages, and add-ons
- [FAQ](https://scopebnb.com/faq): experience needed, weather guarantee, what you receive, targets, subscription
- [Blog](https://scopebnb.com/blog): guides and field notes on astrophotography under dark skies

## Facts
- Sky quality: Bortle 1 (darkest class)
- Clear nights: ~270 per year
- Managed imaging: $65 to $100 per night (priced by sky darkness), delivered within 24 hours
- Remote control: sold only by the block, 3 nights for $150 or 7 nights for $300 (best value, most popular); flat rate, no moon-based pricing
- Integrated image add-on: $25
- Equipment: wide-field rig, ~3° × 2° field of view
- No subscription; weather guarantee with free rescheduling
